raw.comments:
Edit only Tablet/PowerCopiedTerminates.tex. Preserve the Lean statement, imports, and support DAG; do not add a helper. The current proof jumps from the legal-move facts to "this process reaches a pair of atoms after finitely many steps" without defining the pair sequence or showing the contradiction with well-foundedness. Cite 
oderef{PowerCopiedFailureMove}, 
oderef{PowerMove}, 
oderef{PowerGameDescent}, and 
oderef{PowerGameDescentWellFounded}; explicitly name the adjacent copied pair at each depth, split the case where the first coordinate is a node from the case where it is already an atom, and show that every nonterminal successor is a PowerGameDescent predecessor. Then argue by accessibility that an infinite nonterminal continuation is impossible, yielding a finite k, and match the resulting atom pair and depth to 
oderef{PowerCopiedTerminalAt}. Keep the badness/failed-pair condition from PowerCopiedFailureMove visible, but do not use the proof of any cited node. No statement/import/support changes.
